analysis.title: US Daily: October GSAI: All Tricks, No Treats
key_insights: The Goldman Sachs Analyst Index (GSAI) fell 6.5pt to 49.1 in October, below 50 for the first time since April 2025. The composition was mixed-to-weak.
The new orders component fell 33.0pt to 29.5, its lowest since May 2020. The shipments component rose 17.3pt to 58.1 and the employment component fell 1.6pt to 50.6.
The exports component rose 10.0pt to 60.0 and the inventories component fell 13.2pt to 36.2. The orders less inventories gap fell 19.8pt to -6.7.
Other business activity surveys were mixed to stronger on net. GS's manufacturing survey tracker rose 0.2pt to 56.1 and its services survey tracker rose 0.6pt to 53.8.
The employment component of the manufacturing tracker rose 0.5pt to 53.0 while the services tracker's employment component fell 0.6pt to 50.2.
Price components of the GSAI rose to high levels: materials prices +5.0pt to 80.0, wages +3.2pt to 71.4, output prices +20.7pt to 81.8.

Prices received in business surveys have risen substantially in manufacturing and more moderately in services. Some of the strength in survey tracker levels reflects nominal bias, but price-adjusted trackers still look solid.

In the Philadelphia Fed special questions, 52% of manufacturing firms and 44% of services firms expect total 2027 capex to increase vs 2026. Another 48% and 30%, respectively, expect it to stay roughly the same.

By category, manufacturers expect capex to rise on net in every category. Services firms expect software and hardware spending to rise on net but energy-saving investment and structures spending to fall on net.

In GS's special question on top risks to 2027 outlooks, concerns tied to the war in Iran (input cost inflation, supply disruptions) were cited most often. AI spending and adoption risks were also top of mind, with slowing demand and elevated interest rates cited less often.
GS notes that a GSAI of 50 appears more consistent with trend growth than with no growth. Survey responses were collected October 19-23.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Fell 6.5pt and moved below 50 for the first time since April 2025. GS says 50 is closer to trend growth than to no growth.
Fell 33.0pt to the lowest since May 2020, the main driver of the headline decline.
Fell 13.2pt. The orders less inventories gap fell 19.8pt to -6.7.
